story: Bhima, the second Pandava and son of the wind god Vayu, was the strongest of the brothers and had an enormous appetite. He killed demons like Hidimba and Bakasura, and after Draupadi's humiliation he vowed to break Duryodhana's thigh and drink Dushasana's blood. He kept both vows.
belief: He is remembered as fierce, loyal and simple-hearted, with a special devotion to Draupadi. He was also a great cook.
turns: He struck Duryodhana below the waist in their mace duel, breaking the rules of fair combat. His temper and violent vows made him feared even by his own allies.
facts: He and Hanuman are both sons of Vayu, so they are brothers.
During the year in disguise he worked as Ballava, the royal cook.
His son Ghatotkacha, born to the rakshasi Hidimbi, fought for the Pandavas.
